tests.description: Non-destructive probe for PHP SOAP XXE by requesting a WSDL over HTTP and checking for XML parser error behavior. This does NOT attempt to read local files.
tests.expected_indicator: If a SOAP endpoint exists and is vulnerable to unsafe external entity handling, the response or server error logs may show attempts to fetch the external WSDL URL. From the client-side, indicators include detailed XML parser errors mentioning remote URL resolution rather than a simple 404/not-found or generic error. Absence of any SOAP or XML-related response suggests no publicly reachable SOAP endpoint at this path.

tests.description: Safe check for misconfigured PHP SOAP WSDL caching by invoking a SOAP-style path and looking for path disclosure or cache-related error messages. This does not attempt to write or modify files.
tests.expected_indicator: If a SOAP service is exposed and misconfigured, the response may include PHP warnings/notices referring to soap.wsdl_cache_dir or open_basedir paths, or show full filesystem paths. A generic 404/HTML page with no PHP warning text suggests this specific issue is not exposed at this location.

tests.description: Check if /admin is an exposed panel or directory listing that could enable further attacks. Non-destructive, read-only request.
tests.expected_indicator: If vulnerable, the response may show an unauthenticated admin dashboard or an Apache directory index listing files under /admin. A login page requiring credentials or a 403 response suggests a lower risk for direct unauthenticated access.

tests.description: Verify that Apache server-status is properly restricted and does not leak internal information. Uses only a read-only GET.
tests.expected_indicator: A secure configuration should return 403 Forbidden or redirect to an authenticated area. A detailed Apache status page showing current requests, IPs, and server configuration details would indicate information disclosure and misconfiguration.

tests.description: Non-destructive reflected XSS probe via crafted path segment often used with prettyPhoto or similar lightbox plugins. Only checks for JavaScript execution in the tester's browser; does not store payload or attack other users.
tests.expected_indicator: If vulnerable, the response HTML or resulting DOM will render the injected </script><script>alert('pp-xss')</script> unencoded, causing a visible alert dialog in the tester’s browser when the page loads. Properly secured applications will HTML-encode or safely handle the path, preventing script execution.

tests.description: Generic test for reflected XSS in query parameters often parsed or manipulated by jQuery. Proof-of-concept only, triggers an alert in the tester’s browser if reflected unsanitized.
tests.expected_indicator: If vulnerable to reflected XSS at this entry point, the page will cause alert('jq-xss') to execute in the tester’s browser when loaded with this URL. Correctly implemented output encoding will show the payload as plain text or encoded entities instead, with no JavaScript execution.

tests.description: Check for sensitive path disclosure via robots.txt. Non-destructive and read-only.
tests.expected_indicator: If present, robots.txt may list disallowed admin or backup paths (e.g., /admin/, /backup/, /old/, /private/) that could be investigated further. A 404 or minimal robots.txt with only generic Disallow rules indicates limited information disclosure from this file.

tests.description: Probe for verbose PHP error messages or phpinfo exposure, which can make legacy PHP 5.2.17 more exploitable. Non-destructive; does not attempt to upload or modify anything.
tests.expected_indicator: If phpinfo.php exists and is accessible, the response will contain a full PHP configuration page with detailed version and environment info, which is an information disclosure issue. A 404, 403, or redirect to a generic page suggests no direct phpinfo exposure at this path.
